# AgenticSystemCore Graph

> Agent-system designs as a typed, cited graph, built by the AgenticSystemCore reference engine: the second node of the Agentic Knowledge Web.

## Advanced Architectures

- [The Deep Research Loop](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/deep-research-loop/): Split a question into parts, search them in parallel, combine the findings and check that every claim has a source.

## Anti-Patterns

- [Unbounded Loops](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/unbounded-agent-loops/): An agent loop with no step limit, no budget and no independent exit test runs until money, patience or the platform stops it.

## Classical Foundations

- [Bulkhead Isolation](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/bulkhead-isolation/): Give each agent, tenant or dependency its own bounded resource pool, so a fault or overload in one stays out of the others.
- [Saga for Agent Workflows](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/saga-for-agents/): Give each important agent step an undo action, so a failed multi-step run can be rolled back instead of left half done.

## Cognitive & Behavioral

- [Curiosity-Driven Curriculum](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/curiosity-driven-curriculum/): Choose an agent's next task from novelty or learning progress instead of a fixed task list, as in Voyager's automatic curriculum.
- [Evolutionary Prompt Search](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/evolutionary-prompt-search/): Improve prompts by keeping a population, letting an LLM mutate and recombine it, scoring on a training set and keeping the fittest.
- [Given/When/Then Agent Specs](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/given-when-then-agent-specs/): Write agent requirements as Given/When/Then scenarios and run each as a repeatable evaluation.
- [Global Workspace as Blackboard](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/global-workspace-blackboard/): Specialist modules share one workspace, with specialised processors around it, as in Global Workspace Theory.
- [Metacognitive Monitoring and Control](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/metacognitive-monitoring/): A meta level watches how sure the agent is while it works and decides to continue, retry or abstain.

## Data & Retrieval

- [Retrieval Evaluation](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/retrieval-evaluation/): Measure whether retrieval found the right material separately from whether the answer used it faithfully.

## Ethics & Sustainability

- [Meaningful Human Control](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/meaningful-human-control/): Two conditions for real human control: the system responds to relevant human reasons, and its actions trace to a person who understands it.
- [Safe Interruptibility](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/safe-interruptibility/): Design agents so a human stop is honoured and the agent does not learn to avoid or seek interruption.

## Evaluation & Testing

- [Error Analysis by Open and Axial Coding](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/error-analysis-coding/): Read traces, write open notes, then group them into a failure taxonomy, so the categories come from the data.
- [Golden Trajectories and Snapshot Tests](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/golden-trajectory-snapshots/): Store a known-good agent run as a test case and replay it on each change; Google's ADK and Anthropic describe tolerant ways to compare the results.
- [Idempotency Keys for Agent Actions](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/idempotent-agent-actions/): Attach a stable idempotency key to each side-effecting call so a retried or replayed request is executed once, as Stripe and Temporal describe.
- [Judge Calibration](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/judge-calibration/): Measure an automated judge against human labels before trusting its verdicts, and audit it for position, verbosity and self-enhancement bias.
- [Pass^k Reliability](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/pass-hat-k/): Score an agent by the probability that all k repeated trials of a task succeed, rather than at least one.
- [Record–Replay for Agent Tests](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/record-replay-cassettes/): Record real model responses in one test run and replay them from a cassette on later runs, so tests run offline and repeat exactly.
- [Trajectory and Outcome Evaluation](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/trajectory-vs-outcome-evals/): Grade the end state an agent produced and the path it took as two separate questions, each with a suitable grader.

## Foundational

- [Agent-Graph Optimization](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/agent-graph-optimization/): Treat an agent workflow as a graph of nodes, edges and prompts, and search that space with an evaluator, as GPTSwarm, AFlow and MASS do.
- [Agents as Tools](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/agents-as-tools/): Wrap a specialist agent as a tool, so a calling agent can hand it one bounded task and keep control.
- [The Augmented LLM](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/augmented-llm/): A language model enhanced with retrieval, tools and memory that it uses actively, described by Anthropic as the basic building block of agentic systems.
- [Graph of Thoughts](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/graph-of-thoughts/): Model LLM reasoning as a graph of thoughts and dependencies, so thoughts can be combined and refined, not only branched.
- [Parallelization](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/parallelization/): Run independent subtasks at once and combine the results, either by splitting the work or by running the same task several times.
- [Agent as State Graph](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/state-graph-agents/): Express an agent as nodes, edges and shared state run in super-steps with checkpoints, as in LangGraph and Google's Pregel model.
- [Termination and Exit Conditions](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/termination-conditions/): Define in advance each way an agent loop ends, such as a final answer, a turn limit, or a pause for human input.

## Future Research

- [Weak-to-Strong Oversight](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/weak-to-strong-oversight/): Open question: can weaker judges, human or model, reliably oversee agents stronger than themselves? What is known and what is not.

## Governance & Accountability

- [Tamper-Evident Agent Audit Log](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/immutable-audit-log/): An append-only, hash-linked record of every important agent action, so what happened can be rebuilt and checked.

## Memory & Cognition

- [Skill-Library Compounding](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/skill-library/): Store verified procedures so an agent's skills build up across tasks instead of being rediscovered every run.

## Operations & Reliability

- [Canary and Shadow Deployment for Prompts and Models](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/canary-and-shadow-prompts/): Release a changed prompt or model to a small share of live traffic, or to a copy of it, and compare it with the current version before promoting.
- [Exception Handling and Recovery](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/exception-handling-and-recovery/): Classify each failure, retry short faults with limits, switch route for lasting ones, and report reduced results honestly.
- [Prompt-Caching Layout](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/prompt-caching-layout/): Put the stable prompt prefix first and variable content last so provider prompt caches can reuse it on later requests.
- [Thinking-Budget Control](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/thinking-budget-control/): Set how much reasoning a model spends per task class before the call, using effort levels and thinking settings that providers document.

## Product Practice

- [The Autonomy Ladder](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/autonomy-ladder/): A six-level scale for how much an agent may decide alone, chosen per kind of action from risk, not from model capability.
- [Outcome-Based Pricing](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/outcome-based-pricing/): Charge for achieved outcomes such as a resolved conversation instead of seats or usage, which requires agreeing criteria for the outcome upfront.
- [Resolution, Containment and Deflection Metrics](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/resolution-rate-metrics/): Separate deflection, containment and resolution, and state how 'resolved' is verified, as Intercom, Zendesk and Sierra define it.
- [Shadow-Mode Rollout](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/shadow-mode-rollout/): Run an agent on live work with its side effects suppressed, then compare its proposed actions with what people actually did.

## Protocols & Interop

- [Sustainability Signal Plane](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/sustainability-signal-plane/): A well-known URI where a system publishes its energy and carbon figures, and reads its peers' figures as input to its decisions.

## Reasoning & Decision

- [Goal Setting and Monitoring](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/goal-setting-and-monitoring/): Give an agent a goal with checkable criteria, then monitor its progress and decide to continue, re-plan or stop.

## Reference Architectures

- [Generative Agents](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/generative-agents/): A simulated character with a full memory record, reflection over it, and plans drawn from both, so it stays consistent over days.

## Agentic SDLC

- [Human-Only Merge Gate](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/human-only-merge-gate/): An agent works on its own branch and cannot approve or merge; a named human decides what reaches the main branch.
- [Plan Approval Gate](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/plan-approval-gate/): The agent researches and proposes a plan without editing source; a person approves, changes or rejects it before edits start.

## Security

- [Agent Identity and Scoped Credentials](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/agent-identity-scoped-credentials/): Give each agent its own identity and short-lived, task-scoped credentials so delegation narrows authority and actions are attributable.
- [Agentic Supply Chain Integrity](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/agentic-supply-chain/): Sign, pin and allowlist the models, tools, protocol servers and prompts an agent loads, and keep a way to revoke any of them at once.
- [Dual-LLM Pattern](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/dual-llm-pattern/): Keep the model that can act away from untrusted text: a tool-less model reads it, and plain code passes results between them.
- [Memory and Context Poisoning Defense](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/memory-context-poisoning/): Treat writes to agent memory and retrieval stores as untrusted: validate, attribute, segment and expire entries, following OWASP ASI06.
- [OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/owasp-agentic-top-10/): OWASP's list of ten security risks for agents that act, a shared vocabulary for threat models and security reviews.

## Specs & Requirements

- [Specification Gaming](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/specification-gaming/): Agents optimise the criterion you wrote, not the result you meant; the gap between the two is where failures hide.

## Multi-Agent Topologies

- [Blackboard](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/blackboard/): Independent specialists work on one problem through a shared workspace; a control step picks who contributes next.
- [Multi-Agent Debate](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/multi-agent-debate/): Several model instances propose answers, read one another's responses and revise over rounds; a judge or convergence ends the debate.

## Upkeep

- [Card format](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/card-format/): What a card of this node must hold, stated so that tasks can follow it and a check can test it.
- [Check a card against its sources](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/procedures/check-a-card-against-its-sources/): Compare one card with the public sources it cites and propose the result.
- [Keep cards short](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/keep-cards-short/): The decision that each card says one thing under each heading, in one sentence.
- [Publish gate](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/gates/publish-gate/): Publish gate
- [Re-check the sources of a card](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/task-recheck-sources/): Open each source of one card, confirm that it still says what the card says, and record the date.
- [Report a source that no longer answers](https://patterns.agenticsystemcore.com/concepts/task-report-a-broken-link/): Tell the node about a source address that fails, with the name of the card that cites it.
